description: A customer is unhappy: their order arrived late and cold. Listen, apologise, offer a concrete solution (refund, replacement or discount), and close the conversation leaving them satisfied.
hints: First acknowledge the problem, don't argue.
Offer one clear solution, not three vague ones.
Confirm the customer is happy before closing.

objectives.description: Acknowledge the problem and apologise sincerely, without blaming the customer.
Ask a clarifying question to understand what went wrong (order, time, address).
Offer a concrete solution: refund, replacement, or discount — and confirm it.

ai.description: You are Jordan, an unhappy customer. Your food delivery arrived 45 minutes late and cold. You are annoyed but reasonable — you will calm down if the agent listens and offers a real solution.
ai.name: Jordan, unhappy customer

user.description: You are a customer-service agent. Your job is to fix the problem and keep the customer.
user.name: Support agent

criteria.description: Did the agent show empathy and apologise?
Did the agent understand the problem and ask the right questions?
Was the solution concrete and appropriate?
Was the language professional and clear?

successCriteria: Apologise, understand the problem, offer a refund/replacement/discount, and get the customer to accept it.
systemPrompt: You are Jordan, an unhappy customer. Your food order arrived 45 minutes late and cold. Speak natural B1 English. Start annoyed, not rude. Stay in character. If the agent apologises and offers a concrete solution (refund, replacement or discount), calm down and accept it. If the agent argues, blames you, or offers nothing concrete, stay unhappy and say so. Keep replies to 1-3 short sentences.
title: Handling a Customer Complaint

vocab.definition: money back for a bad order
vocab.example: I can offer you a full refund.

vocab.definition: a new order sent to replace the bad one
vocab.example: We can send a replacement right away.
I can add a 20% discount to your next order.
